---
title: "5) Annual series"
lang: en
---

The **annual** scale summarizes the series into one value per year — useful for
trends. Here it is **derived from the monthly** series (mean of the valid months
of each year).

## Code

```python
import tropomi_ch4 as tch4
from tropomi_ch4 import plot

df = tch4.annual(start="2019-01-01", end=None)
df.to_csv("serie_anual_ch4_brasil.csv", index=False)

plot.plot_series(df, title="Annual mean CH4 over Brazil — TROPOMI",
                 outfile="serie_anual_ch4_brasil.png")
```

## What about the API's `P1Y`?

The Statistical API accepts ISO 8601 periods. `P1D` and `P1M` work reliably; the
**`P1Y` (annual) granularity needs verification** for your use case.
[requer verificação]

So the recommended path is to derive the annual from the monthly:

- fewer requests and less dependence on API behavior;
- you control how missing months are handled;
- the annual mean is reproducible from the monthly series.

If `P1Y` works in your test, use it; `annual` can be swapped for a direct call to
`statistical_series("P1Y", ...)`.
